item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission commissioned research on Queensland council employees’ corruption perceptions to monitor prevention work and inform future planning.
item.support:
so the CCC can 
monitor the impact of its prevention agenda and 
inform future strategic planning.

item.text: An online survey received 973 completed responses between 28 March and 9 May 2025.
item.support:
An online survey of Queensland local council employees was 
conducted between 28 March and 9 May 2025.

item.text: The CCC reported that policy non-compliance and mishandling confidential information were the highest perceived workplace corruption risks.
item.support:
The behaviours considered the highest risk include 
non-compliance with policies and procedures and 
mishandling of confidential information

item.text: The CCC reported that 55% said they had witnessed or suspected corruption in the preceding five years, and 48% of that group did not report it.
item.support:
Over half (55%) of local council employees have either witnessed, or 
think they have witnessed, corruption in the past 5 years.

item.text: The CCC reported that 73% intended to report corruption, while 46% expected personal repercussions and 40% doubted meaningful action would follow.
item.support:
Local council employees are sceptical as to 
whether meaningful action would be taken if 
they report corruption

item.quote:
The reporting of corruption among those who have witnessed or 
suspected it in the past 5 years is varied.

Local council employees are sceptical as to 
whether meaningful action would be taken if 
they report corruption, with four in ten 
believing this would not be the case (40%).
